expected_return.window: scorebord: BUY 13:30 ET on the entry day; SELL amc at the next open, bmo at 13:00 ET on the report day; gross

note: Each member is reported as a percentile of its own live range, 0-100 (pct), with its direction in side; panel_pct (0-100) is the size of the mean of the signed percentiles and side its direction; panel_pct_sd their spread. The selection is panel_pct in the top 20%. panel_score is the signed median of the members' sizes, each read against its own recent history. consensus_k counts members that put the name in their own top 20% on the panel's side; that, not sign agreement, is what selected well on the development names. Certainty (p_up) is recorded and decides nothing. expected_edge_pct is a shrunk in-sample prior, not a forecast. Research only.

opus5.note: The two-year stack arithmetic off a much tougher base (Q3 2025 company SSS +3.3% with a September bagel festival and a delivery-subsidy boost, against Q2 2025 -3.6%) points Q3 2026 company SSS near -24% from -17.3%, with marketing spend guided up 'significantly' from September into an already 5.7% contribution margin (i=0, i=3); the offsets are that there is no consensus bar to miss, the stock is already -40% since the August print at a $14k-a-day tape (i=4), Luckin's monthly-improvement commentary supports a constructive exit rate (i=1) and RBI's milestone-conditioned $55m note programme is still funding it (i=2) — so a negative lean on inference, not a decisive one.

opus55.note: Lean down on items 0 and 3: the tougher Q3 2025 comp points to SSS worse than Q2's -17.8%, and the guided marketing ramp widens the EBITDA loss. Both are inferences, partly priced after a 40% fall, and Luckin's monthly improvement (item 1) offsets them in part.

sonnet55.note: Tougher Q3 comp (company SSS +3.3% last year) likely worsens SSS and margin (items 0, 3), partly priced by a 40% drop; Luckin exit-rate and RBI funding partly offset.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0 (Q3 SSS laps a +3.3% bagel-festival base, so the two-year stack implies about -24%) and item 3 (guided marketing ramp widens the EBITDA loss), both inferences and partly in a stock down 40% since August; item 1's Luckin monthly improvement is the small positive, bar unsourced so sizes capped.

opus5.note: The Nov 18 Soleus royalty sale ($5.6M against a ~$7M cap) plus removal of the $4M BlackRock minimum-cash covenant makes the Q3 release the first scheduled runway/cash statement since, on a name trading near net cash (i=0); the runway extension itself is the hunter's inference and an unfinished August-offering seller (i=1) is actively selling into it, so the lean is modest and abs_move is set on this nano-cap's own ~7-8% print reactions, raised for understatement.

opus55.note: Rests on item 0: the Nov 18 royalty sale and covenant removal make a runway extension and cash near the $7M market cap the likely new content (inferred, not company-stated), partly offset by the unfinished-seller tape in item 1.

sonnet55.note: Rests on the inferred runway extension and net cash near the $7M cap after the royalty sale (item 0), offset by a possibly unfinished seller (item 1); no bar, no options, thin tape.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0 (first runway update since the $5.6M royalty sale, with net cash near a ~$7M market cap and prints bought 3 of 4) against item 1 (an unfinished news-free seller on a $26K/day tape); both are inferences, the bar is single-sourced, so the lean is small.

opus5.note: Q3 is the first full quarter of the higher Rio Grande charter with the 20.5 Q2 off-hire days gone, 100% 2026 coverage and no drydocks until 2027, against trailing quarters and no published estimate for anyone to be positioned on (i=0) — but the reaction function here is the sanctions language, not the revenue line: a repeat of the Nov 3 'no assurance replacement services will be available' wording six weeks before the Jan 1 UK ban on 34.5% of revenue (i=1) plus a $50M preferred redemption out of $59.5M of June cash (i=3) cap the lean, so p_up stays close to 50 and the clean read is only mildly positive.

opus55.note: Small long lean on item 0, the first full quarter of the accretive Rio Grande charter at a 52-week low with no bar, tempered by the UK sanctions restatement and a thinner post-redemption cash cushion (items 1, 3).

sonnet55.note: First full quarter of the higher Rio Grande charter (item 0) against a Jan-1 UK sanctions cliff and a $50M preferred redemption thinning cash; no consensus, sanctions risk mostly priced.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0: first full quarter of the accretive Rio Grande charter on a 100%-covered fleet with no Q3 off-hire, clean quarters having been bought (+5.5%) while the units sit at the 52-week low on sanctions headlines; item 1's UK sanctions restatement is the offset and the bar is unsourced, so everything is capped small.

opus5.note: Street revenue consensus ($7.83-7.90m) sits at or above the top of the company's own $7.7-7.8m guide, which requires Solutions (62% of revenue, two quarters flat with stated renewal pricing pressure) to hold >= $4.8m against a $5.1m comp, and the Oct 15 KPI release changed its Solutions wording from 'will be discussed' to a hedge (i=1); the exact same setup — pre-released KPI beat with revenue lagging estimates — printed -13.9% in Q3 2025, and the GBV beat itself has been public five weeks (i=0), with a possible reverse-split disclosure on top (i=4).

opus55.note: Near balance: the pre-released Platform KPI beat (item 0) against soft Solutions with hedged wording and a consensus at the top of the guide (item 1); the name's reaction history has gone both ways on the same setup.

sonnet55.note: Pre-released KPI beat is mostly priced and offset by soft Solutions line and the Q3-2025 precedent of KPI beat then -14%; roughly balanced.

fable51.note: Rests on item 1: the company's own Oct-15 KPI release changed its Solutions wording to a hedge while street consensus sits above the top of the $7.7-7.8m guide, the same shape as Q3 2025 (KPI beat pre-released, revenue lagged, -13.9%); item 0's Platform beat is five weeks public and partly offsets.

opus5.note: The baseline's 5.38% event-implied move is the thing that most clearly does not hold — ordinary realised vol is 128%, one day is 8.1% and the last print closed -16.92% — so abs_move is set at 17; direction is genuinely two-sided and nets mildly positive: a hard, dated 46.0m-ADS short (16% of ADS, ~26% of float ex-CATL, 6.9 days to cover, put/call OI 0.18) after a 43% twenty-day collapse to the 52-week low (i=3) is the repo's own twice-measured squeeze setup, Tencent's RMB81.4bn and Alibaba's RMB50.5bn capex prints landed in the three days before this call and after VNET last spoke (i=2), and management committed in August to present its strategy and outlook in Q4 with a 38.1% CATL-linked holder that paid $8.69 adding a director on Nov 16 (i=6) — against a well-built but inferred 2-4% revenue miss and FY-guide trim (i=0, i=1) that this name has sold hard before.

opus55.note: The run-rate arithmetic says Q3 revenue misses a roughly RMB3.0bn bar and the FY guide gets trimmed (items 0 and 1). This is largely offset by a crowded short (about 26% of float) into a capitulation of -28.6% over 5 days with call-heavy open interest (item 3), so the lean is only slightly down.

sonnet55.note: Q3 revenue likely 2-4% under a RMB3.0bn bar and FY guide trim risk (items 0, 1; Q2 in-line print fell 17%) against a crowded, capitulated short at -43% in 20 days (item 3) and hyperscaler capex proxy.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0 (a RMB3.0bn consensus needs +8% QoQ against a +3.3% Q2 run-rate and a 'marginally faster' move-in guide, in a sector that sold a slight miss -16.9% in August) against item 3 (16% of ADS / ~26% of float short, call-heavy OI, -57% since the last print, which is the squeeze mechanism); the 5.4% option event move is far below one day at 128% realised vol, so abs_move sits near the last print's size.
